audit.why: 50.34% over 294 games against a chart that gives Olaf levels 2-3 and both item stages and leaves 1, 4-5 and 6 as Skill. A dead-even headline built from an Olaf-favoured opening and close with Camille's true-damage window in between is coherent, so nothing moved.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text is broken text that shipped to the page: it argues with itself mid-sentence - 'he's CC-immune and walks out of nothing but still can't be locked... wait, he still can't leave, but he ignores your E-stun, so save E too.' It reads as an unfinished draft. No Olaf cooldown appears anywhere either, so 'only when Ragnarok is down' has no clock.
audit.why: Ragnarok is 100/90/80s, Undertow a flat 9s, Tough It Out 16/15/14/13/12s, Reckless Swing 11/10/9/8/7s. The 100s on Ragnarok at rank 1 is the entire plan of this matchup and it was never stated.
audit.corrected: spikes[2].text is rewritten as one clear instruction with Ragnarok's 100s attached; mid and whys[4] carry the same number.

audit.whatIsWrong: The central claim of the matchup is wrong in five places: 'Ragnarok turns his BASIC ATTACKS into true damage'. Ragnarok gives armour and magic resist passively and, on activation, immunity to disables - there is no true damage anywhere in it. His true damage is Reckless Swing (E, 11/10/9/8/7s), a single-target hit that also costs him health. Three more omissions: the disable immunity lasts only AS LONG AS HE KEEPS ATTACKING, so it is not a fixed window; Berserker Rage scales his attack speed and lifesteal off his MISSING health, so he gets stronger the lower he goes; and Undertow reduces ARMOUR as well as move speed. Tough It Out (W) - an attack-speed steroid with a shield - is never mentioned at all. Camille's passive is spelled 'Adaptive Defense'; it is Adaptive Defenses.
audit.why: Riot, Ragnarok: 'Olaf passively gains increased armor and magic resist. He can activate this ability to become immune to disables for as long as he keeps attacking.' Reckless Swing: 'Olaf attacks with such force that it deals true damage to his target and himself.' Berserker Rage: 'Olaf gains Attack Speed and Life Steal based on his missing Health.' Undertow: 'reducing their Armor and Move Speed.' Tough It Out: 'Olaf's Attack Speed is increased and he gains a Shield.'
audit.corrected: spikes[0], spikes[3], mid, late, whys[0], whys[6] and wants.foe[1] now put the true damage on Reckless Swing, describe Ragnarok as attack-conditional disable immunity, name the missing-health lifesteal scaling, and add Undertow's armour shred and Tough It Out's shield.

audit.why: The anti-heal call is already there and correctly timed - Executioner's early, Mortal Reminder or Chempunk later - which is right because Berserker Rage's lifesteal is a permanent passive rather than an ult effect.

edits.after: Hextech Ultimatum (R) isolates Olaf in a 1v1 you can win — but fire it only AFTER Ragnarok. While that 100s ult is active he is immune to disables for as long as he keeps swinging, so your Hookshot knock-up and the R anchor both do nothing. Hold both, let him burn it, then commit.

edits.before: Level 1 is Olaf's — his Undertow (Q) slow plus passive lifesteal out-trade your single ability, so don't contest the first wave; walk over the thrown axe to deny him the slow and the pickup. Note his Q is physical, not true, so it's only Ragnarok that beats your shield later. Once you have W and a point in E you stabilize: chip with the W outer edge, which deals max-HP damage and heals you off him, and only commit to a trade when his Ragnarok (R) is on cooldown.
edits.after: Level 1 is Olaf's — Undertow's slow and armour shred plus a lifesteal that scales with his MISSING health out-trade your single ability, so don't contest the first wave; walk over the thrown axe to deny the slow and the pickup. His Q is physical, so it is Reckless Swing's true damage that beats your shield, not his autos. Once you have W and a point in E you stabilize: chip with the W outer edge for max-HP damage and the heal, and only commit when Ragnarok is down.

edits.before: This is your window to even the lane. With Q ranked, lead the W outer edge as Olaf steps up to last-hit, weave the empowered Q2 true damage, then peel out on your move-speed boost before the trade goes long and his lifesteal wins. Hold E for a wall-stun ONLY when Ragnarok is down — if you E in and he Ragnaroks, your stun is ignored and you're stuck in a melee grind where his autos turn true. At 6, R isolates him in a 1v1 you can take, but cast it after his Ragnarok, never into it.
edits.after: This is your window to even the lane. With Q ranked, lead the W outer edge as Olaf steps up to last-hit, weave the empowered Q2 true damage, then peel out on your move-speed boost before his lifesteal wins the long trade — it grows as his health falls. Hold E for the wall knock-up ONLY when Ragnarok is down, because while he keeps attacking through it your CC is ignored. At 6, R isolates him in a 1v1 you can take, but cast it after that 100s ult, never into it.

edits.before: It evens to a coin-flip, then tips back to Olaf at full items — he's an elite reckless duelist whose lifesteal out-sustains your tempo once the fight goes long, and Ragnarok's true-damage autos shred you through your shield. Anti-heal (Executioner's into Mortal Reminder, or Chempunk) is mandatory or you simply can't close the duel. Only ego-duel him in the side lane with R up and items even; otherwise use E to flank through walls and lock his carries with R in skirmishes instead of grinding Olaf 1v1.
edits.after: It evens to a coin-flip, then tips back to Olaf at full items — he's an elite reckless duelist whose lifesteal climbs as he drops, and Reckless Swing's true damage shreds you through your shield while Ragnarok blanks your CC. Anti-heal (Executioner's into Mortal Reminder, or Chempunk) is mandatory or you simply can't close the duel. Only ego-duel him in the side lane with R up and items even; otherwise use E to flank through walls and lock his carries with R in skirmishes rather than grinding Olaf 1v1.

notes: TWO SERIOUS PROBLEMS. First, spikes[2].text shipped as visibly unfinished draft text that contradicts itself mid-sentence ('...walks out of nothing but still can't be locked... wait, he still can't leave, but...'). That is on the live page. Second, 'Ragnarok turns his BASIC ATTACKS into true damage' is wrong in five places - Ragnarok has no damage component at all; it is armour/MR plus disable immunity, and the true damage is Reckless Swing. A player building armour against 'true damage autos' is being told the opposite of what to do. Two details that change how you fight him were also missing entirely: Ragnarok's immunity only holds WHILE HE KEEPS ATTACKING, and Berserker Rage's lifesteal and attack speed scale off his MISSING health, so the low-HP Olaf you are trying to finish is the strongest one. Tough It Out (W), a shield plus attack-speed steroid, appears nowhere in the matchup.
